metaDescription: Shark cordless vacuums compared across the lineup, from the Pet stick and Vertex Pro to the Freestyle Max and auto-empty dock, by head, battery and upkeep.
expertTake: The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus IZ382H is the best all-round Shark because the head adapts to the floor and the housing is sealed. The Pet IX141AMZ is the value pick with a big cup. Skip the premium tiers if you only clean a small flat; a plain Pet stick covers it for much less.
introParagraphs: This maker sells more cordless models than anyone else, and the names blur together: Pet, PowerPro, PowerDetect, Vertex, Freestyle and Clean and Empty. The useful way to sort them is by head design, battery plan and whether a dock empties the bin.

Most buyers are choosing between a plain workhorse, an adaptive head, a two-battery long-runner, a light upright and a self-emptying system. Knowing which of those you need matters more than the model number.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus IZ382H cordless stick
products.description:
Within this brand's range, the IZ382H is the model where the head does the most thinking. It senses whether the floor is carpet or hard and slows or speeds the roller to match, so one stick covers rugs and tile without a mode change. A flex joint lets the wand bend under low furniture, and the lights show dust that is hard to see at standing height.

The PowerFins roller sheds hair as it spins, and the sealed housing keeps fine dust inside the machine. Next to the Pet IX141AMZ it is the more automated and cleaner-running stick, though the IX141AMZ has the bigger cup, and next to the Vertex Pro it is lighter but has only one battery.

In practice the chores are a monthly filter rinse, a wipe of the sensor windows and a check of the flex joint for hair. Spare batteries and filters for this platform are widely sold, which is the quiet reason people stay with this brand for a second and third machine. One habit pays off with floor-sensing heads: pause a beat when you roll from tile onto a rug, so the sensor can settle before you push on, and if the roller seems stuck in the wrong mode, lift the head and set it down again, which resets the reading far more often than a trip to the manual.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors where the head should manage itself.
pros: Roller speed adapts to the floor
cons: Sensors and flex joint need keeping clean
Costs more than the Pet stick

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty IP3251 with auto-empty dock

specList.label: Dock
specList.value: Seals dirt away, listed up to 45 days

products.description:
The IP3251 is the one to buy if you never want to open a dirty bin. Park the stick and the base pulls the contents into a sealed chamber, so you handle dust only when the chamber is full. A head that detects dirt and edges raises suction where it is needed and settles back to save battery.

Compared with the IZ382H it adds the dock and the dirt-detecting head but is heavier overall and needs a base on the floor. The listed forty-five days of dirt capacity assume light use, and a shedding pet will fill it faster.

Upkeep moves to the dock: wipe its intake and seals every few months, rinse the stick's filters and check the roller for hair, since the dock empties the bin but not the brush. Give the base a clear spot away from hallway traffic so it is not knocked over. Dock the stick firmly until it seats, since a half-seated stick leaves the bin partly full, and listen for the short evacuation burst that tells you the system ran. When the chamber is finally full, empty it into a bag held tight to the opening, outdoors if anyone in the house is sensitive to dust.
products.bestFor: People who dislike handling dust and have space for a base.
pros: Dock empties the bin when you park
Head raises power on dirt and edges
cons: Roller hair still needs manual clearing

products.name: Shark Vertex Pro IZ682H with 2 removable batteries
products.description:
The Vertex Pro answers the main weakness of every cordless stick: running out of charge. It ships with two removable batteries that the maker rates at a combined 120 minutes, so a big house can be finished with a mid-clean swap. A DuoClean PowerFins head with a self-cleaning brushroll covers carpet and hard floor and sheds hair.

The maker says it delivers the performance of a full-size vacuum in Boost mode, a comparison with one of its own uprights, so treat it as a claim about relative strength. Compared with the IZ382H it is bigger and heavier but has far more runtime, and compared with the Freestyle Max it is a stick rather than an upright.

Rotate the two packs so they age evenly, wipe the contacts every few months and rinse the filters on schedule. The removable handheld handles stairs and furniture, and it is an older design, so confirm the current battery listing before relying on it for years. Because the two packs sit in a shared holder system, put a fresh pack in first when you start a big clean, and keep the second on the charger so the swap is a thirty second pause rather than a wait, and label each pack with a date so you can see which one is aging faster.
products.bestFor: Large homes that want a spare battery in the box.
cons: Heavier and bulkier than the lighter sticks
Combined runtime is a low-mode figure

products.name: Shark Freestyle Max cordless upright SV2002

specList.label: Power
specList.value: Strongest multi-surface cordless in the brand

products.description:
This is the brand's cordless take on an upright: a wide head, a body that rolls on wheels and a weight under seven pounds. The maker calls it its most powerful multi-surface cordless, which makes it the pick for open rooms where a narrow stick means many passes.

The tradeoff is reach. It does not convert and slide under furniture the way a stick does, so stairs and ceilings need another tool. Compared with the Pet IX141AMZ it covers floor faster, and compared with the Vertex Pro it relies on one pack.

Check the roller for hair, rinse the filters monthly and park it upright. Its weight rides on the wheels, so it feels lighter in use than a stick of the same mass, which suits people with tired wrists. Because the head is wide, check that it clears chair legs and door frames in your home, and lift it over thresholds instead of dragging it, since the wheels and the roller housing are the parts most likely to scuff a skirting board. Store it upright with the battery on the charger, and avoid leaning it against a wall where it can slide.
products.bestFor: Open living areas with large rugs and little stair cleaning.
cons: Less reach under furniture and on stairs
Single battery for a wide head

products.name: Shark Cordless Pet IY143H with self-cleaning Turbo Pro roll

specList.label: Hair
specList.value: Removes long hair as it cleans

products.description:
Where the IX141AMZ uses a plain bristle roller, this model uses a Turbo Pro brushroll that cleans itself while it works. Long hair is stripped off as you go, and FloorDetect trims the speed on bare floors so fur does not scatter.

That makes it the better stick for a long-haired pet, and the more expensive one. Compared with the IZ382H it is more pet-specific and less sealed, so choose it for hair and the IZ382H for allergens.

Rinse the filters monthly, check the roller ends every few weeks and keep the head clear of pebbles. The forty minute rating is a best case, so plan on less on carpet. Even a self-cleaning roller can let a few strands slip to the bearing end, so look there every few weeks, and if a long-haired household sees the motor note drop, stop and clear it before the motor strains, since a stalled roller drains the pack faster than any boost button.
products.bestFor: Long-haired pets on a mix of carpet and hard floor.
pros: Roller strips hair while you clean
Floor sensing slows the brush on bare floor
cons: Costs more than the plain Pet stick

products.name: Shark Pet cordless stick IX141AMZ with XL dust cup

specList.label: Runtime
specList.value: Up to 40 min, standard mode, hand vac

products.description:
The Pet stick is the plain workhorse of the range: a bristle roller, accelerated suction, an extra-large cup and LED headlights. It has no sensors, so there is little to fail, and the hand unit comes off for stairs.

The forty minute figure is measured at the hand vac in standard mode, which is closer to real use than an eco claim. Next to the IY143H it wraps hair more and costs less, and next to the Freestyle Max it is narrower but far more flexible.

Wash the filters monthly, cut hair from the roller ends and store the stick upright. For a flat or a first Shark, it is the sensible place to start. The big cup is easy to empty into a bin because the wide mouth lets a clump of hair drop out whole, and the hand unit means the same stick can handle the car and the stairs, so a single purchase replaces two. Keep the crevice tool and the pet tool in one bag with the stand so that neither goes missing.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want the simplest, best-supported Shark.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The IZ382H and IY143H use self-cleaning rollers with FloorDetect, the Vertex Pro uses DuoClean PowerFins and the Pet IX141AMZ uses a plain bristle roller. Hair handling and floor behavior come from the head, not the motor. Choose the head for your floors and pets first, and remember that the same motor can feel very different under a different head, so a model that looks like a small step up on paper can be a large step in how often you have to stop and cut hair from the roller.

The Vertex Pro ships with two removable batteries rated at a combined 120 minutes, while the IZ382H and Freestyle Max have one pack. A big home needs a second pack or a bigger bin. Shark sells replacement packs, so a spare is easy to add, and a second pack for a single-battery model is usually a cheaper way to double your working time than stepping up to a more expensive stick, so price the spare before you decide that you need the two-pack model.

The Clean and Empty IP3251 empties its bin into a sealed base, listed for about 45 days of light use. That saves handling dust but adds a base and weight. A stick without a dock is lighter and cheaper, and the dock only helps if you actually park the stick on it, so think honestly about whether you will, and whether the floor space for the base is available in the room where you keep the vacuum.

The IZ382H and IZ363HT advertise an anti-allergen complete seal, and the IP3251 pairs HEPA with a sealed dock. The plain Pet stick does not make the same claim. If allergies matter, choose a sealed model, wash the filters on schedule and empty the bin or the dock outdoors, since even a sealed system releases a little dust at the moment of emptying and the filter holds the finest particles collected over weeks.

The Freestyle Max is a cordless upright under seven pounds with a wide head. The others are sticks that convert and reach furniture. Pick the shape that matches your cleaning, not the brand name: a home with stairs and low furniture wants a stick, while one with a single large living room and bare feet on the rug may be happier with the upright and its wheels, and a household with both can reasonably own one of each.
The Pet stick states its forty minutes at the hand vac in standard mode. The Vertex Pro's 120 minutes is combined across two packs. Stronger modes cut every figure sharply, so compare like with like.

cards.label: Stick
cards.text: The IZ382H, Pet IX141AMZ and Vertex Pro convert and reach furniture and stairs, but cover less floor per pass.

cards.label: Cordless upright
cards.text: The Freestyle Max covers floor quickly with a wide head and wheels, but lacks reach for stairs and ceilings.

howToChoose.note: Choose a stick for variety and an upright for open rooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A self-cleaning roller, a big cup and a sealed filter for dander. Check roller ends monthly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The IY143H has the self-cleaning Turbo Pro roller, and the IZ382H adds a sealed system. The Pet IX141AMZ has the biggest cup.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have mixed floors, allergies or a big home. The IZ382H, IP3251 or Vertex Pro each remove a specific chore.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small home. The Pet IX141AMZ covers daily cleaning.

maintenance.why: Even self-cleaning rollers let some hair through.
A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry fully before refitting.
Dust confuses sensors and causes charging faults.
Using one pack more ages it faster.
A dirty seal weakens the empty cycle and lets dust escape into the room. Wipe the rubber lips with a dry cloth and replace any that look cracked.

faq.a: The IZ382H is the best all-round for mixed floors and allergies. The Vertex Pro is better for big homes that need a spare battery.

faq.q: Is the auto-empty model worth it?
faq.a: If you dislike handling dust, yes. The IP3251 base adds weight and floor space, and listed days of capacity assume light use.

faq.q: How long do Shark batteries last?
faq.a: Lithium-ion packs fade in two to five years. Shark sells replacement packs for these models.
A sensor that adjusts the brushroll speed to carpet or hard floor so crumbs do not scatter.

faq.q: Is the Freestyle Max better than a stick?
faq.a: It covers floor faster, but a stick reaches stairs and furniture, so the better choice depends on whether your rooms are large and open or small and cluttered with low furniture.
They are low-mode or combined figures. Expect less on carpet or boost.
